<strong>Vous n’avez toujours pas trouvé: Still haven't found an apartment on the eve of moving day? Resources exist to support you, help you avoid ending up without a roof over your head and assert your rights. Here are the main steps recommended by the organizations working on the ground.
Pour les intervenants, le conseil est un: For frontline workers, the advice is unanimous: don't wait until the last minute. “Anyone who still hasn't found housing today should dial 311 to access our services. The sooner we can support households, the better,” says Valérie Rhême, director of the communications department at the <l1>Office municipal de l’habitat de Montréal (OMHM)</l1>, in a response sent to our newsroom.
L'appel permet d'être dirigé vers le Ser: The call connects you to the housing search assistance service, which can support households through the process and, when necessary, give them access to emergency measures.
Le <l1>Front d’action populaire en réamé: The <l1>Front d’action populaire en réaménagement urbain (FRAPRU)</l1> makes the same recommendation. “In Montréal, we encourage people to contact 311 as early as possible so they can be directed to the right resources. If they don't get help, they can then reach out to FRAPRU or their local housing committee,” says Ms. Lussier.
<strong>Des aides souvent méconnues</str: Forms of help that are often overlooked
Au-delà de l'hébergement temporaire, plu: Beyond temporary accommodation, several measures remain little known.
L'OMHM rappelle que les ménages peuvent: The OMHM points out that households can receive, among other things, personalized support, help storing their belongings and help with moving. This year, a new partnership also makes it possible to have the pets of sheltered households looked after temporarily, an obstacle that sometimes kept people from accepting an emergency solution.
L'organisme met aussi à la disposition d: The organization also provides the public with a tool to search for available units on the private market, accessible on its website.
Les deux organisations insistent égaleme: Both organizations also stress the importance of consulting a housing committee before signing any document or leaving a unit following a repossession or an eviction. “Many tenants don't know about housing committees,” says the OMHM, which recommends contacting one for information about tenants' rights and available recourse.
Le FRAPRU rappelle que plusieurs ménages: FRAPRU notes that many households face discrimination during their search, particularly immigrants, racialized people and people with low incomes. In a highly competitive market, some also accept illegal demands, such as security deposits, for fear of losing the only available unit.
Pour le FRAPRU, les mesures mises en pla: For FRAPRU, the measures put in place by municipalities are essential to prevent households from sliding into homelessness.
« Ces mesures sont nécessaires, mais ell: “These measures are necessary, but they're a Band-Aid on a much bigger wound,” says Catherine Lussier. The organization is calling in particular for more social housing, better rent control and a mandatory rent registry to preserve long-term affordability.
En attendant, les intervenants lancent l: In the meantime, frontline workers have the same message for households still searching for housing: ask for help quickly rather than waiting until July 1. Several resources exist, but they can step in more effectively when they are contacted before the situation becomes an emergency.

Si les organismes insistent autant sur l: The reason organizations insist so much on asking for help quickly is that the housing crisis continues to hit low-income households hard.
À Montréal, le taux d'inoccupation attei: In Montréal, the vacancy rate has now reached 3.1%, but this improvement doesn't benefit everyone. “What we notice a lot on the ground is really the lack of affordability of what's on offer on the market. There are more units available, but it's mostly the most expensive ones that are being offered for rent,” sums up Catherine Lussier. Low-income neighbourhoods remain hard hit by the crisis. <l1>In Saint-Michel, for example, 79% of households were tenants in 2020, and more than a third devoted a high share of their income to rent.</l1>
Selon des données transmises à <em>La Co: According to data provided to La Converse by the OMHM, 720 requests for help had been processed as of June 28, compared with 796 at the same point last year. The organization was still supporting 226 households in their rehousing efforts, and 54 were already in temporary accommodation.
L'OMHM estime que <strong>64 ménages mon: The OMHM estimates that 64 Montréal households will be without housing on July 1. Ten others were expected to move into temporary accommodation between June 28 and moving day. The organization considers, however, that this picture is now relatively stable, as needs are generally well documented at this stage of the year.
À l'échelle du Québec, la Société d'habi: Across Quebec, the Société d'habitation du Québec had recorded, a few days earlier, 3,186 households that had asked for help finding housing, including 144 already in temporary accommodation.
Les personnes seules et les familles mon: Single people and single-parent families remain the hardest hit, according to FRAPRU and the OMHM.
